source: OpsHarness (Huang et al. 2026) From General Agents to RCA Experts
finding: Bare general agents (Codex, Claude Code) beat hand-built RCA agents. The authors say the remaining gap is missing system-specific expertise, like a skilled newcomer who lacks the team's experience.
numbers: Overall top-1: Codex GPT-5.5 51.2% (OpenRCA 44.9, RCAEval 57.4); mean over 4 backbones 36.1% for the bare agent vs 17.9% RCA-Agent vs 5.6% mABC. RCAEval: RCA-Agent 5.1% vs bare agent 38.0%.
quote: a bare flagship general-purpose agent is already often better than prior RCA agents
limits: Preprint, one group. Four backbones, two benchmarks. Own harness is the proposed system.
agent_relevance: Supports a thin scaffold on a strong model. The gap to experts is stored experience, not reasoning.

source: OpsHarness (Huang et al. 2026) From General Agents to RCA Experts (self-evolution)
finding: Letting the harness mine past diagnoses (success and failure) into reusable knowledge, skills and tools made accuracy climb with use. Static harness stayed flat.
numbers: Final A@1 averaged over 4 backbones: full 59.0%, no-evolve 41.4%, ICL 38.4%, Direct 36.1%. Cold-start substrate +5.3 pts, self-evolution +17.6 pts, total +22.9. 12 windows: full climbs about 0.4 to 0.9 on GPT-5.5; final-window A@1 0.83 full vs 0.43 no-evolve.
quote: what compounds is mined experience, not raw recall of past cases
limits: Windows reuse training splits of the same benchmarks (same-system setting). Gains are in-system, not cross-system.
agent_relevance: Direct machine analogue of expert schema building. Memory should store distilled rules, not raw past episodes (matches S0 memory design).

source: OpsHarness (Huang et al. 2026) From General Agents to RCA Experts (ICL vs distilled)
finding: Retrieving three correct past rollouts into the prompt (few-shot ICL) barely helped. Distilled best practices helped much more.
numbers: ICL 38.4% vs Direct 36.1% final A@1; overall Avg Score 67.0% vs 68.8% (ICL slightly worse). Cold-start substrate lifted weakest model DeepSeek-V4 from 20.3% to 31.6%; on GPT-5.5 only 51.2% to 52.8%.
quote: retrieving similar rollouts injects raw examples but not distilled, reusable best practices
limits: Gain from experience is smallest on the strongest model at cold start.
agent_relevance: Warns against a memory that is just a case store. Store abstractions with a trigger condition.

source: OpsHarness (Huang et al. 2026) From General Agents to RCA Experts (verification gate)
finding: Unchecked self-updates overfit and then hurt accuracy. A held-out regression gate kept the gains.
numbers: No-verify final-window A@1 0.33, below no-evolve 0.43. DeepSeek-V4 no-verify fell from peak 0.4 to 0.0. 37% of proposals rejected by the gate; accepted ones took 1.7 attempts on average. Example: up-weighting network anomalies helped source cases and broke CPU/memory cases.
limits: Weaker models mine spurious patterns more. Gate needs a disjoint held-out testbed.
agent_relevance: Strong support for G3 and for gated memory writes: a stored lesson must pass a held-out check before it is kept.

source: OpsHarness (Huang et al. 2026) From General Agents to RCA Experts (cost and artifacts)
finding: Self-evolution cost is comparable to a bare agent because experience cuts trial and error. Fine-grained rules fire rarely but precisely.
numbers: About 106k tokens and 325 s per case vs Direct 112k and 317 s. Evolved artifacts (recall/precision %): workflow skeleton 91.7/73.5, operation skill 82.5/84.3, note-rule 64.7/85.1, persisted tool 61.0/77.2.
limits: Per-case cost excludes separate evolve and verify stages, which the paper reports apart.
agent_relevance: Layered memory: broad workflow skeletons plus narrow high-precision rules.

source: Lu et al. (2026) Beyond Fault Localization: trajectory-level study of LLM agents for microservice RCA
finding: Open-ended, adaptive investigation frameworks win; constrained pipelines lose. Backbone model matters more than framework among top agents.
numbers: 10 framework-backbone configs, 5,000 trajectories. ThinkDepth.ai 79.2%, AIQ 77.6%, ClaudeCode 79.6% Acc@1; TaskWeaver 65.2, RCLAgent V2 53.4, GoS 48.2, OpenRCA 46.6, OpsAgent 45.8, mABC 42.6. Sonnet ThinkDepth 90.0%, +10.8 pts over Qwen; top-3 frameworks span only 2.0 pts.
limits: Single microservice system (RCABench); authors flag external validity.
agent_relevance: Do not hard-wire the diagnostic sequence. Let the model choose what to look at, with code only checking and budgeting.

source: Lu et al. (2026) Beyond Fault Localization: trajectory-level study of LLM agents for microservice RCA (causal depth)
finding: Accuracy falls with causal-chain depth for weaker models; correct answers still rest on partial causal maps. Edges are harder than nodes.
numbers: Depth 2 to 5: ClaudeCode(Qwen) 89.5 to 57.1%, AIQ 86.8 to 42.9%; Sonnet ThinkDepth 85.7 to 96.8% flat. Edge F1 never above 0.67; mABC Node F1 0.41 vs Edge 0.09. From correct to incorrect runs Node F1 drops 16-43%, Edge F1 43-69%.
limits: Process labels from manual path annotation; reviewer agreement 97.4% (kappa 0.59) on 500 graphs.
agent_relevance: A right final answer is not proof of a right mechanism. Check the causal chain, not only the label (G3).

source: Lu et al. (2026) Beyond Fault Localization: trajectory-level study of LLM agents for microservice RCA (budget)
finding: More rounds did not mean better diagnosis. Failed runs ran longer than successful ones.
numbers: Incorrect runs used up to 11.4 more rounds than correct ones; top agents used 45-54 rounds, over 1500 ktok, about $0.2 per case. Incorrect runs trail on both F1 metrics too.
limits: Correlational.
agent_relevance: Supports stopping on signal (impasse detector) rather than on a fixed long budget; long runs often mean drift.

source: Lu et al. (2026) Beyond Fault Localization: trajectory-level study of LLM agents for microservice RCA (intent repertoire, expert-like search)
finding: Successful runs use a richer set of SRE-style diagnostic intents and use evidence to guide the next query. Weak runs loop on a few moves.
numbers: Sonnet ran resource_probe in 82.8% of trajectories vs 16.6% for Qwen. Fault-type gaps: Resource 75% vs 94%, JVM code 66% vs 93%; Network 82% vs 89%, HTTP 88% vs 87%. Qwen acts on the prior result on 24.9% of rounds vs 54.3% for Sonnet.
limits: Intent labels coded by LLM with sampled human checks (about 98% agreement on 1,000 labels, kappa 0.73).
agent_relevance: Machine version of the expert-novice split: breadth of moves and using the last result. Both can be checked in code from traces.

source: Lu et al. (2026) Beyond Fault Localization: trajectory-level study of LLM agents for microservice RCA (failure catalogue and DiagGuard)
finding: Recurring failure modes: omitted evidence, misread evidence, unsupported reasoning (anchor lock, silence read as healthy). A small rule-based guard cut them.
numbers: Silence-as-health in 30% of the Sonnet failure pool; anchor lock 28% in one row. DiagGuard raised Acc@1 in all 14 configs: median +10.5 pts on RCA100 (range 3.5-35.1); mABC +21.1/+35.1 from 35.1%/3.5%. MIS3 did not drop (11.8% to 13.6%).
limits: Rules were mined on the same benchmark family, then tested on 2 held-out sets.
agent_relevance: A failure-mode checklist mined from traces works as a novice-to-expert patch. Fits G2 and G10 (anchor lock, overconfidence).

source: Gong et al. (2026) ORCA-bench: How ready are language model agents for oncall?
finding: Frontier coding agents do poorly on realistic oncall RCA, and hallucinate a cause when evidence is missing.
numbers: 1,079 tasks, 50 GB of six-day telemetry. Best RCA accuracy 25.3% Medium, 10.0% Hard. Weakest model hallucinates an implausible cause in 40% of reports (40.2). Judge-human Cohen's kappa 0.91.
limits: Single public microservice system; authors say real production is far larger.
agent_relevance: Expect low base accuracy without system knowledge. Require evidence for any named cause (G2).

source: Gong et al. (2026) ORCA-bench (source code access)
finding: Removing source code access cut accuracy and raised hallucination for every model. Knowledge of the system is a lever, as in experts.
numbers: RCA accuracy drops 9-16 pts without code. Incident-time accuracy stays robust (Opus 4.7 82.6% to 79.9%).
quote: removing source code access reduces RCA accuracy and increases the hallucination rate for every evaluated model
limits: Same testbed caveats as above.
agent_relevance: Giving the agent a structural model of the system is worth double-digit points: argues for a system-model slot in memory.

source: Bi et al. (2026) Free to Look, Free to Reason
finding: Simple harnesses that leave the model free to choose evidence beat published hand-crafted RCA agents on the same 90 cases.
numbers: RCAtlas: 90 validated cases from 8 datasets, 6 models, 3 effort levels. Simple harnesses PR@1 65-77% on three mid-tier models; published LLM agents 16-53%; non-LLM methods 6-39% (best NSigma 38.9%).
limits: 90 cases only; single-pass noise on weak models (Codex 62/69/76% across 3 passes on Luna).
agent_relevance: Scaffolds that prescribe the expert's SOP can skip the decisive evidence. Keep prescriptions to checks, not to the search path.

source: Bi et al. (2026) Free to Look, Free to Reason (capability vs effort vs multi-turn)
finding: A stronger model gives reliability, a multi-turn loop gives aptitude, more reasoning effort gives little.
numbers: Luna to Sol: PR@1 +14-18 pts, calls fall (Codex 16% to 12% of entities queried). Effort up: +2-4 pts at 1.5-4x wall time (up to 7x in abstract). Multi-turn solves 10-11 pts more cases at least once than one-shot; one-shot never solves 26% of cases vs 14-16% for agents. Sol passes differ by at most 4.5 pts.
limits: Authors note this is the opposite of Laban et al. (multi-turn mainly costs reliability).
agent_relevance: Spend budget on tool-using iteration and verification, not on longer thinking per step.

source: Zha et al. (2026) Trace2Policy: from expert behavior traces to self-evolving decision agents (EISR)
finding: Rules distilled from expert practice plateau near 70% in one shot. Error-driven refinement with a regression gate lifts them. Rule quality, not model size, was the lever.
numbers: One-shot distillation about 70% across 5 LLMs; 8 EISR rounds reach 79.6% (77.3, 76.8 on other sets) as compiled Python with zero LLM calls. Production 22 days, 3,349 audit cases; pure-LLM baseline 72.7%; same content 9.8 pts higher as Python than as prompt. Auto-EISR $5-$10 per cycle vs 70 expert-hours. Per-round accuracy not monotonic (R5 crash 90% to 70%).
limits: Logistics audit, skewed base rates, not fault diagnosis; re-enabling LLM fallback lowered accuracy in this calibrated setting. Industry report, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Tacit expert rules can be recovered by error clustering (MISSING, WRONG, CONFLICT) and gated commits. Fits rule-writing into S0 memory.

source: Hu and Ash (2026) Chat Debugging: human-AI collaboration to debug analog circuits
finding: Undergraduates used public LLMs on a 30-minute hands-on circuit-debugging exam. LLMs gave useful domain knowledge but misread images and spoke with unjustified confidence. Students lacked basics and critical checking.
numbers: 17 usable chat logs (5 Spring 2025, 12 Fall 2025), 6 fault types; classes of 60 and 40 students. Qualitative thematic analysis only. Example: model claimed 99% confidence on wrong op-amp pins.
limits: Voluntary self-selected logs, no stats, one university, no control group. Authors note experts lean on experience while novices have none.
agent_relevance: A novice plus an overconfident model compounds errors. Agent must show evidence behind confidence (G10).

source: Fang et al. (2026) OpenRCA 2.0: from outcome labels to causal process supervision (PAVE)
finding: Final-answer RCA scores hide ungrounded diagnoses: models find a correct service but cannot show the causal path.
numbers: 500 instances, 11 frontier LLMs. Exact root-cause set recovered in 20.7% on average. At least one correct service in 76.0%; grounded in a verified propagation path in only 61.5%.
quote: agents identify at least one correct root-cause service in 76.0% of cases
limits: Fault-injection microservice data; abstract and intro read, not full text.
agent_relevance: Pattern matching can stand in for diagnosis. Score and require the mechanism, not just the label (G3).

source: Qi et al. (2026) R2Act: recovery-aware evaluation of diagnosis-to-action reasoning
finding: Right diagnosis does not give right repair. Models diagnose well but pick invalid recovery actions.
numbers: 302 Kubernetes incidents. Best RAG LLMs 91.4-99.7% root-cause service accuracy but recovery validity only 36.8-60.3%. Given correct service and fault type, invalid actions still chosen in 39.5-62.0%. Live replay: 146 of 302 Qwen-RAG predictions valid and recovered.
limits: Abstract and intro read; one app (Online Boutique).
agent_relevance: Test the fix (check that repair works), because naming the fault is the easy half.

source: Luo et al. (2026) Rethinking tool design for agentic RCA
finding: Higher-level tools save time but do not always help; extra evidence can make agents override a correct recommendation.
numbers: 375 failures, 3 systems, 8 configs. Qwen3.7-Plus: L3 82.8% top-1 localisation vs 85.4% for L0 Python reference, in under half the time. Adding L3 helped three models but hurt Qwen3-8B, which rarely invokes L3. Rankings differ across systems.
limits: Abstract read; one model family.
agent_relevance: Pre-digested expert tools help only if the model uses them and does not talk itself out of them.

source: Jansson et al. (2026) Supporting industrial test-failure analysis with LLM-based systems
finding: At Westermo, a single agent matched an orchestrated multi-agent system in practitioner-rated quality, and was faster and cheaper.
numbers: 2 failure scenarios, 6 practitioners, 120 repeated runs. No consistent quality advantage for either configuration.
limits: Tiny sample, two scenarios, exploratory.
agent_relevance: Multi-agent role splitting (mimicking expert teams) gave no clear gain; supports single-agent design.

source: Gott, Bennett and Gillett (1986) Models of technical competence for intelligent tutoring systems
finding: Early AI/tutor work building expert troubleshooting models for tutors. Named in the subfield row; recalled from memory.
numbers: No numbers taken this session.
limits: Not opened. No URL verified. Human-side angles should cover it.
agent_relevance: Source of the claim that experts hold a system model plus strategies, to be checked by other angles.

source: Lesgold et al. (1992) Sherlock: coached practice environment for an electronics troubleshooting job
finding: Older AI tutoring system for avionics test-station troubleshooting, built from expert-novice contrasts. Recalled from memory.
numbers: No numbers taken this session.
limits: Not opened. No URL verified.
agent_relevance: A scaffold built from expert behaviour can lift novices; compare with the machine harnesses above.

source: de Kleer and Williams (1987) Diagnosing multiple faults (General Diagnostic Engine)
finding: Keeps competing fault hypotheses and picks the next probe by expected entropy. Recalled from memory.
numbers: No numbers taken this session.
limits: Not opened. DOI from memory, unverified. Model-based diagnosis is another subfield.
agent_relevance: Probe choice by information gain is an expert-like move that code can compute.

source: Laban et al. (2025) LLMs get lost in multi-turn conversation
finding: Cited by Bi et al. (2026) as finding that splitting a task over turns mainly costs reliability. Bi et al. found the opposite for RCA agents.
numbers: Not read; only the citing paper's description.
limits: Not opened. No URL verified.
agent_relevance: Multi-turn is a risk when the model must track its own state; tool-grounded turns differ.
